claim: For physician non-competes, it requires a buyout capped at the physician's total annual salary and wages at termination, expiration no later than one year after termination, and a geographic limit of no more than a five-mile radius from the physician's primary practice location.
evidence: Non-compete buyouts for physicians are capped at the physician’s total annual salary and wages at termination. Non-compete restrictions must expire no later than one year after termination of the physician’s contract or employment. Non-compete agreements must limit the restricted area to a five-mile radius from the physician’s primary practice location at the time of termination.
excerpt:
Non-compete buyouts for physicians are capped at the physician’s total annual salary and wages at termination.

Buyout cap: The buyout provision, which allows a physician to pay to be released from the non-compete, is capped at the physician’s total annual salary and wages at the time of termination. This replaces the previous “reasonable price” standard and eliminates the option for arbitration to determine the buyout amount.

Temporal limitation: Non-compete restrictions must expire no later than one year after termination of the physician’s contract or employment.
